children: International cotton prices rose in August, says Cotlook in a note. The firm says that its global price index rose to $1.013 a pound in August, which is the highest prices have been since May 2024. Driving the rising price is a host of factors, says Cotlook. "Bolls were opening in the key Xinjiang region, but uneven development was reported," says the firm. "Crop conditions deteriorated in the U.S. under hot, dry weather." The USDA will be releasing its next WASDE report at noon Eastern time, which will contain the latest production data for U.S. cotton crops. ICE cotton futures are down 1.1% to 87.26 cents a pound, but have gained 36% year-to-date. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
